entries.speaker: Cognitive Wakaba Isshiki
entries.en: A monster born of Futaba Sakura's cognition.[n]As sphinxes ordinarily guard enshrined kings[n]or gods, she may have been protecting Futaba.

entries.speaker: Yaldabaoth
entries.en: God of control, born of the human subconscious.[n]Gnostic lore describes Yaldabaoth as a false, evil[n]god who crafted this physical world.

entries.speaker: Adam Kadmon
entries.en: Maruki's evolved Persona. The Kabbalah[n]describes Adam Kadmon as a primordial[n]human with a deific form—an ideal for all[n]to strive towards.

entries.speaker: Arsène
entries.en: Joker's heart given form by his rebellious will.[n]Known as a master of disguise, though it's all born[n]from keen observation and behavioral mimicry.

entries.speaker: Captain Kidd
entries.en: Ryuji's heart given form by his rebellious will.[n]Based on the infamous privateer William Kidd.[n]Of the man's early life, no official record exists.

entries.speaker: Goemon
entries.en: Yusuke's heart given form by his rebellious will.[n]He appears in many stories set in the Edo period,[n]but he actually lived during a different era entirely.

entries.speaker: Necronomicon
entries.en: Futaba's heart given form by her rebellious will.[n]The Necronomicon, also called the "book of the[n]laws of the dead," appears in H.P. Lovecraft's work.

entries.speaker: Robin Hood
entries.en: Akechi's heart given form by his rebellious will.[n]Stories paint Robin Hood as a legendary vigilante,[n]but he may be a fanciful amalgam of other figures.

entries.speaker: Loki
entries.en: Akechi's heart given form by his rebellious will.[n]In Norse mythology, Loki is a trickster god and[n]shapeshifter, sometimes appearing as a woman.

entries.speaker: Cendrillon
entries.en: Sumire's heart given form by her rebellious will.[n]Cendrillon is a French form of Cinderella, derived[n]from the French for cinders: "Cendre."
